decisions.reason: Requiring a reusable full-pin breakout does not change the three-board partition, the main board's role within this project, or its exclusions.
The full-pin through-hole breakout requirement does not alter the existing requirement to place the ESP32 antenna at the PCB edge.
The client explicitly establishes that the main-board form factor must provide routing space, not merely component-placement space, while retaining through-hole access to every ESP32-S3 pin.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Understood—the available routing space is important as well, rather than only the component placement. I also want to retain the ESP32 through-hole breakout, since I intend to reuse this main board as a general ESP32-S3 base platform in other projects involving a display, MCU, and buttons. Having access to every pin is a hard requirement for me.
Do you have any suggestions, such as changing these to 1.25 rather than 2.54?

value_updates.routing_space_requirement: provide sufficient space for routing rather than only fitting components
value_updates.breakout_routing_constraint: retain through-hole access to every ESP32-S3 module pin

decisions.reason: The source decision concerns the ESP32 breakout and routing on the main board, not the power board's dimensions, orientation, mounting, or connector placement.
The discussed through-hole pitch concerns the ESP32 pin breakout and does not change the placement or alignment rules for the separate-board JST connectors.
The main-board ESP32 breakout decision does not change the power board's four-layer stack or grounding strategy.
Providing through-hole access to every ESP32-S3 pin does not change the standalone USB regulator, powered loads, source selection, or activation condition.
Breaking out every module pin preserves physical access but does not reassign any functional GPIO or change the confirmed candidate GPIO pool.
The breakout coverage and format do not change the I2C cable, speed, pull-up, or series-resistor requirements.
The full-pin breakout decision does not alter the switched 5V rail's GPIO assignment, loads, converter, or operating behavior.
The ESP32 breakout requirement has no necessary effect on DCDC1 voltage regulation or Schottky-drop compensation.
The general reference to projects involving buttons does not modify the existing panel reset connector, electrical action, or physical implementation.
